# Cntxt Labs

> Cntxt Labs (also written cntxt, pronounced "context") is a small software company in New Zealand, founded by Cristian Rus and operating since 2017. It designs and builds apps for iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, for the web and for Android. More than 1.75 million people around the world have downloaded its apps.

This is the complete text of https://cntxtlabs.co, written for language models and agents. Every page is here, so there is no need to crawl the site to answer a question about it. The About page (https://cntxtlabs.co/about), in full:

Cntxt Labs is a small software company, founded by Cristian Rus in 2017. It designs and builds apps for iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, for the web and for Android, and more than 1.75 million people around the world have downloaded them.

For more than ten years the work has been about how design changes what people do. The company picks an everyday problem, builds the simplest thing that solves it, and keeps improving it for as long as people rely on it. Left helps people see their time. txtpod turns reading into listening. SafePlate replaces the paper food safety diary in New Zealand kitchens. KiwiCamping and AussieCamps find a place to camp without signal, and NoSnus helps people stop using nicotine pouches.

Most of the apps run on your phone, need no account and do not track you. When an app needs more than that, its own privacy policy says exactly what it does and why.

Alongside its own apps, Cntxt Labs designs and builds apps and websites with a small number of other teams. Write to info@cntxtlabs.co about working together.

## Contact

The best way to reach Cntxt Labs is by email, at info@cntxtlabs.co. It is the only address the company uses, and it is read every day by the people who build the apps, not by a support desk.

If something isn't working in one of the apps, say which app it is, which device and version of iOS you are using, and what happened. That is usually enough to sort it out in one reply. Ideas are just as welcome, and a good number of the features in the apps today started as an email.

Press, review copies, promo codes and partnerships go to the same address. Journalists and reviewers are answered first.

## Products

### Left

Left is built on one idea: your time is limited, and seeing it changes how you use it. It shows the year, the month, the week, the day and your whole life as symbols that dim as they pass, on your Home Screen, Lock Screen and StandBy.

Then it helps you act on what you see. Build habits on any schedule and protect the streaks that matter. Track any goal you can count with Aim, from money saved to books read, and let Apple Health fill in the progress for you. Share a habit or a streak with a friend and keep each other going.

Ahead holds the dates that pull you forward, like trips, birthdays and deadlines, each with its own to-do list, and you can count down to them together with friends. The Planner brings your habits, dates, calendar, reminders, weather, sleep and workouts into one calm view of the day, and a simple fasting timer follows you on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.

More than 1.5 million people use Left on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/left
- Website: https://getleft.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/left-widgets-for-time-left/id6740155884
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch
- Privacy policy: https://getleft.app/privacy

### SafePlate

Food businesses in New Zealand have to keep records: fridge temperatures, deliveries, cooking and cooling, cleaning, training and staff sickness. In most kitchens that still means a paper diary, often filled in late and hard to find when the verifier arrives.

SafePlate replaces the diary. The team records each check on a phone as they do it, and everything is kept for four years, ready to show. It works offline and catches up when the signal returns, and one subscription covers the whole team on the web, Android and iPhone.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/safeplate
- Website: https://safeplate.nz
- Platforms: web, Android, iPhone
- Enquiries: info@cntxtlabs.co

### KiwiCamping & AussieCamps

KiwiCamping and AussieCamps help you decide where to stay tonight and where to go next. Each is a camping map and a road-trip planner in one, built the same way: KiwiCamping for New Zealand and AussieCamps for Australia.

Start with the map. KiwiCamping has more than 6,500 places across New Zealand and AussieCamps more than 74,000 across Australia: campsites, holiday and caravan parks, national park sites and free camping areas, along with rest areas, dump stations, drinking water and toilets. Filter for exactly what you need, like free camping with toilets and water nearby, and every place opens with photos, fees, facilities, alerts, the weather and Street View of the entrance.

Then plan the trip. Add the places you like as stops, put them in the order you will drive, and see the distance and driving time for every leg and for the whole journey. Each stop has its own date, notes and forecast, and you tick it off as you go. Keep a packing list beside the itinerary, share it, and sync it to your calendar.

Both apps come with detailed road-trip routes and practical guides, from how DOC sites and freedom camping work in New Zealand to free camps and national parks in Australia. And because the whole directory is stored on your phone, the details are still there after the last bar of signal.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/camping

#### KiwiCamping

KiwiCamping helps you find a place to camp in New Zealand and plan the road trip around it. It has more than 6,500 places, from DOC campsites, huts and freedom camping areas to holiday parks, dump stations and useful stops, and every one is stored on your phone, so it still opens where the signal does not reach.

Filter for what matters on the night, like free camping with toilets and water near Queenstown, and open any place to see photos, fees, facilities, current alerts, the weather and Street View of the turnoff. Save places into collections for a region or a shortlist, and they sort themselves as you mark them liked, starred or visited.

The trip planner is where it comes together. Order your stops the way you will drive them, see the distance and driving time for every leg, add dates, notes and the forecast for each stop, and tick them off as you travel. Keep a packing list beside it and sync the whole trip to your calendar.

KiwiCamping also includes 21 road-trip routes, from Northland to the East Cape, and more than 50 practical guides on how DOC sites, huts and freedom camping work, planning realistic driving days and comparing costs.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/kiwicamping
- Website: https://campingapp.nz
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/camping-map-nz-kiwicamping/id6746952595
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

#### AussieCamps

AussieCamps helps you find a place to stay in Australia and plan the road trip around it. It has more than 74,000 places, from free camps, national park campgrounds and caravan parks to rest areas, dump points, drinking water and toilets, all stored on your phone, so the details are there in the outback, the bush or on a quiet stretch of coast.

Filter for what you need, like free camping with toilets and water around the Gold Coast, and open any place to check fees, rules, access notes, photos, alerts, the weather and Street View. Save places into your own collections, and they sort themselves as you mark them liked, starred or visited.

Then plan the trip. Put your stops in the order you will drive, see the distance and time for every leg and the whole journey, add dates, notes and a forecast for each stop, and tick them off as you go. Keep a checklist and a packing list beside it, share the itinerary and sync it to your calendar.

It also includes 21 Australian road trips and more than 50 guides on free camps, national park campgrounds, realistic driving days and costs. It works the same way as KiwiCamping, with a directory built for Australia, for campervans, caravans, 4WDs, cars and tents.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/aussiecamps
- Website: https://aussiecamps.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6801098680
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

### txtpod

txtpod is for people who save more than they have time to read. It turns articles, links and PDFs into episodes in your own private podcast feed, so the reading list becomes something you can listen to on a walk, a drive or while you cook.

It reads the whole piece, word for word, in a natural voice, with the ads and clutter taken out. It is the article itself, not a summary. Save from the share sheet, the web app or a bookmarklet, or bring in what you already saved in Instapaper, Matter and Readwise. New episodes appear in Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Overcast, Pocket Casts or any other player, next to your regular shows.

There are more than thirty voices across more than twenty languages, and articles in other languages can be translated and read to you in yours. txtpod can also research a topic you are curious about and narrate a full episode on it, or brief you every morning on the subjects you follow. It works on iPhone, iPad and in your browser.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/txtpod
- Website: https://txtpod.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/txtpod-articles-to-podcast/id6748379680
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, web
- Privacy policy: https://txtpod.app/privacy

### NoSnus

NoSnus is built for one thing: getting off nicotine pouches. Zyn, Velo and snus, not cigarettes or vapes. You answer a few questions about how many you use, how strong they are and how soon after waking you reach for the first one, and NoSnus builds a step-down plan with a projected pouch-free date.

Each phase of the plan sets two limits, how many pouches a day and how many milligrams, because fewer pouches at a higher strength is the same nicotine. After the first week the plan recalibrates to what you actually logged, and if a phase is too hard the target moves instead of you failing it. A bad day costs that day, not the week.

Logging takes one tap from a Home Screen widget. Tag what set off a slip, like stress, boredom, driving or a meal, and over a few weeks you see which moments cost you most. When a craving peaks, Breathe walks you through it, and the cravings you get past are counted too, along with the money you are no longer spending.

There is no account, no email and no feed. NoSnus supports a behavioural plan and is not a medical device. If you want clinical support to stop using nicotine, talk to a doctor, a pharmacist or your national quitline.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/nosnus
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/quit-zyn-velo-snus-nosnus/id6791343296
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

### More iOS apps

A few smaller apps, each made for one everyday job in health, habits or time. They run on iPhone, they don't need an account, and they try to stay out of your way.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/ios

#### ftnss

Your watch, your running app and your food log each know part of the story, but none of them tells you what to do next. ftnss reads it all through Apple Health and turns it into advice you can act on.

It looks at your training, sleep, nutrition and recovery, including data from Apple Watch, Strava, Garmin and MyFitnessPal. It builds plans for strength, endurance, mobility and recovery, adjusts them as your week changes, and answers questions about any of it. You can log a meal from a photo or a sentence.

Progress shows up in dashboards for weight, energy and performance, along with your workouts, steps, sleep and longer-term trends.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/ftnss
- Website: https://ftnss.app
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ai-health-insights-ftnss/id6742253667
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch
- Privacy policy: https://ftnss.app/privacy

#### Bites

Most people stop counting calories because logging food takes too long. Bites makes it one sentence: describe what you ate, and Apple Intelligence works out the calories and macros.

It syncs with Apple Health, tracks your daily goal, and shows how much energy you have left once your activity is counted. Meals you eat often can be saved and logged again with a tap.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/bites
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/meal-tracker-bites/id6755179382
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

#### NotSoBusy

Sometimes people need to know when you are free, but not what you are doing. NotSoBusy turns your day or week into a simple picture of busy and free time, without event names or details.

It reads Apple Calendar, Google Calendar and Outlook, and you share the picture in a message or an email. There is no account to create, and your calendar never leaves your phone.

- Page: https://cntxtlabs.co/notsobusy
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/share-schedule-notsobusy/id6745011162
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad

## Privacy

Left, txtpod and ftnss each publish their own policy: https://getleft.app/privacy, https://txtpod.app/privacy and https://ftnss.app/privacy. ftnss sends some anonymised data to an AI model to produce plans and insights; identifiers are removed first.

KiwiCamping, AussieCamps, Bites, NoSnus and NotSoBusy share this policy:

The app runs on your device. There is no account, and no personal data is collected or stored. Purchases go through RevenueCat, which keeps only what it needs to confirm a purchase and restore it if you reinstall the app. Google services are used for crash reports, anonymous usage statistics and a few features inside the app. None of it identifies you, and none of it is sold or shared.

SafePlate is a subscription for kitchen teams and works differently: records are uploaded rather than kept only on the device. The policy above does not describe it. Ask info@cntxtlabs.co for details.

## Common questions

- Who makes these apps? Cntxt Labs, a software company in New Zealand, founded by Cristian Rus.
- How is the name said? "Context". It is written cntxt.
- How do I get support? Email info@cntxtlabs.co and say which app it is.
- Do the apps cost money? They are free to download. Some have paid features, handled through the App Store and RevenueCat. SafePlate is a subscription that covers a whole team.
- Which platforms? iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch. SafePlate also runs on the web and Android, and txtpod has a web app.
- Is there an Android version? SafePlate runs on Android. The other apps are made for Apple platforms.
- Do the apps need an account? KiwiCamping, AussieCamps, Bites, NoSnus and NotSoBusy do not. Check each policy for the others.
- Is Cntxt Labs available for client work? Write to info@cntxtlabs.co about working together.
